newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel seeks 2.5-3.0 bln shekel cut in '98 budget.
newsitem.headline: Israel seeks 2.5-3.0 bln shekel cut in '98 budget.

text.p: Israeli Finance Minister Yaacov Neeman will propose to the cabinet on Sunday a 2.5 ($705 million) to 3.0-billion shekel million) cut in the 1998 budget, ministry sources said.
The proposed reduction was agreed between Neeman, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Bank of Israel Governor Jacob Frenkel at a meeting late on Tuesday.
The government has set a 1998 budget deficit target of 2.4 percent of gross domestic product against 2.8 percent in 1997.
The spending reduction in 1998 would follow nearly eight billion shekels in cuts and revenue raising measures in the 1997 budget.

The sources said the Treasury's proposals for structural reform in 1998, also to be brought to the cabinet on Sunday, will not include any tax measures. The government does not plan to impose new taxes nor does it plan at this time to lower the tax burden, the sources said.
The Treasury and the central bank have not yet managed to settle a dispute over next year's inflation target, Treasury officials said.

The central bank is pushing for a six-to-nine percent target while the Treasury favours leaving the target at its 1997 level of seven to ten percent. The government expects to meet its target this year.
The central bank is seeking to lower Israeli inflation to about four percent by 2001.
While the govenrment fears reducing inflation will lead to a further rise in unemployment the Bank of Israel maintains there is no significant correlation between unemployment and inflation.
